description:
## Outcome

A host-owned resolver maps a requested profile ID to one installed adapter and one trusted profile. Jidoka rejects unknown profiles and any missing required guarantee before external work.

## Why now

Names from data are safe only when trusted host configuration gives them meaning. The validator must exist before a CLI can pass profile selections to Jidoka.

## Current state

CLI `Automation.Plan.runtime_profile/2` maps a name to arbitrary `import_opts` and `run_opts`. It checks shape but not isolation or enforcement. Jidoka has no profile resolver or adapter capability description.

## Ownership and boundary

This is a `jidoka` change. Define a resolver behavior or injected function and a pure compatibility validator. The CLI or embedding host supplies registrations. Agent and scenario data supply only `PolicyRequest` IDs.

## Detailed implementation

1. Add a public `ProfileResolver` contract that returns a trusted `SecurityProfile`, adapter registration, and stable binding fingerprint.
2. Add an adapter capability declaration that uses provider-neutral traits from the data story.
3. Validate the profile against declared adapter capability before `open`.
4. Validate confirmed evidence after every lifecycle call against every required profile dimension.
5. Define typed errors for unknown, disabled, malformed, unavailable, insufficient, and unenforced profiles.
6. Make policy errors stable and projectable. A missing evidence field is not confirmation.
7. Supply a deterministic in-memory resolver for tests, not as trusted production configuration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Only trusted host registrations map IDs to adapters and policy.
- [ ] Unknown, disabled, or ambiguous IDs fail before adapter invocation.
- [ ] Every missing required guarantee has a distinct fail-closed error.
- [ ] Post-call evidence that is weaker than the profile fails even if the adapter returned success.
- [ ] Binding fingerprints exclude credentials and raw commands.
- [ ] Input documents cannot create resolver registrations.

## Test plan

- Success: resolve one complete fake profile and validate full confirmed evidence.
- Invalid input: bad ID, duplicate registration, malformed profile, and unknown capability.
- Runtime failure: resolver raises or adapter registration is unavailable.
- Boundary and security: test each missing isolation, network, workspace, digest, limit, checkpoint, and fork guarantee.
- Deterministic capability: inject resolver and adapter metadata with fixed digests.
- JSONL and exit status: project each typed error as portable evidence; the CLI mapping comes later.

## Documentation

Update the constrained-execution guide with trusted-host resolution, capability matching, and fail-closed examples.

## Non-goals

Do not load host configuration files in Jidoka. Do not start a backend. Do not add CLI flags. Do not infer enforcement from profile requests.

## Dependencies

Blocking issues:

- `jido_cli-tqg.3.2` — Define portable constrained-execution contracts

Features unlocked by this story:

- Execution-environment lifecycle calls
- Data-only profile selection in the CLI
- Capability checks before model or tool work

## Commit plan

Create exactly one focused `jidoka` commit. Use a message such as `feat(jidoka): resolve trusted security profiles (jido_cli-tqg.3.3)`. Do not include another backlog feature.

## Verification commands

```sh
cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jidoka
mix test test/jidoka/execution_environment/profile_resolver_test.exs test/jidoka/execution_environment/validator_test.exs
mix quality
mix test
mix docs
```
title: Resolve trusted security profiles and fail closed
